title: Exec Update — Runtime LTS Channel: GA Plan, Risks, and Staffing (v3)
slides:
01. Title
Runtime LTS Channel — GA Plan, Risks, Staffing
Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)
Exec sponsor: Mateo Alvarez (VP Eng Runtime)
Date: 2025-03-20

02. Why this matters (enterprise reality)
- Dedicated/Private customers want a stable runtime baseline for 6–12+ months
- Incident-driven upgrades are currently a top pain point (latency regressions + behavior drift)
- Regulated buyers require auditable artifacts (checksums/provenance/SBOM) + change control
- Competitive pressure: “serving stability” is becoming table-stakes in RFPs

Key outcomes we’re optimizing for:
- Predictable patch cadence and backport policy
- Performance stability with explicit gates + rollback guidance
- Reproducible and verifiable artifacts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private

03. What we’re shipping (definition of the LTS channel)
LTS is:
- A named release line (runtime-1.18-lts) with monthly patch cadence + out-of-band security patches
- Slower-change release notes (curated, categorized, with known issues + compatibility matrix)
- A clear backport rubric (security/Sev1/Sev2 only, minimal diff, explicit approvals)
- Reproducible, signed artifacts (checksums/provenance; SBOM where applicable)

LTS is not:
- A forked architecture or long-lived divergence from main
- A guarantee of feature parity with mainline

05. Milestones & timeline (proposed)
Phase 1 — Requirements + decisions (DONE)
- ADR approved for branching/versioning
- Release notes taxonomy agreed with Product/CS

Phase 2 — Tooling + gates + packaging (in progress; target complete by 2025-04-12)
- Release branch CI workflows + deterministic builds
- Perf regression gates integrated as release blockers
- Artifact signing/checksum publication + verification docs
- Private installer pinning + Helm values for LTS selection

Phase 3 — Pilot (target 2025-04-15 → 2025-05-15)
- 1–3 enterprise accounts on LTS patch cadence
- Cut 2 consecutive patches (e.g., 1.18.1-lts, 1.18.2-lts) with full process
- Validate support intake + backport request workflow

Phase 4 — GA (target 2025-05-20)
- Publish public docs + internal enablement
- Steady-state monthly patch train + security OOB procedure

06. Scope for GA (what must be true)
GA includes:
- runtime-1.18-lts supported for 12 months (patches) + 3 months overlap window with next LTS
- Monthly patch cadence with published dates (“Patch Tuesday”-style) and comms to Support/CS
- Backport eligibility rubric + approvals enforced (labels + required reviewers)
- Perf gates as mandatory release checks; documented waiver policy
- Signed artifacts + checksums; artifact ↔ commit traceability; SBOM generation available for Private
- Private deployment pinning + rollback steps (installer and Helm)

GA excludes:
- Any new runtime features landing exclusively in LTS
- Guaranteeing identical performance across all customer workloads (we gate on canonical suites + thresholds)

07. Pilot accounts (proposal)
Selection criteria
- High business impact + clear operational pain (change control, upgrade aversion)
- Dedicated or Private deployments (highest need for pinning + artifact verification)
- Willingness to provide benchmark traces and participate in rollback drills

Recommended pilots (from CRM + CS pipeline)
- Northstar Bank (regulated; requires change windows + artifact auditability)
- Helio Health (Private evaluation; SBOM + security posture critical)
- Quantgrid (enterprise SaaS; performance stability + predictable cadence is a deal blocker)

CS owner for pilot comms: Rachel Kim
Support workflow owner: Dev Patel

08. GA criteria (measurable, go/no-go)
Release process readiness
- Two consecutive LTS patches shipped using the runbook end-to-end (no “hero steps”)
- Artifact verification: checksums/provenance validated by at least one Private customer in pilot

Quality + performance
- 0 Sev1 incidents attributable to LTS patch process during pilot
- Perf gates stable: <2% p50 latency regression and <3% p95 regression on canonical suite (or documented waiver)
- No throughput regressions >3% on baseline workloads without documented tradeoff + approval

Operational readiness
- SLO dashboards/alerts for LTS traffic live (SRE) + on-call runbook published
- Support/CS trained on intake + backport request templates
- Comms templates finalized for monthly patches + emergency security patch advisories

09. Risks (top 6) & mitigations
1) Perf gate flakiness blocks release train
- Mitigation: dedicated benchmark runners; rerun policy; variance guardrails; waiver process owned by Release Manager + SRE

2) Backport correctness risk (small diff, big blast radius)
- Mitigation: minimal-diff requirement, targeted regression suites (scheduler + kv cache), mandatory approvals (Runtime lead + SRE), canary rollout

3) Security patch urgency conflicts with change-control
- Mitigation: explicit security patch SLA + expedited approval path; pre-drafted comms; artifact signing automated

4) Private packaging drift (installer/helm mismatch)
- Mitigation: compatibility matrix per patch; installer/helm pinned to exact runtime tag; automated smoke tests

5) Release manager bandwidth (single-threaded)
- Mitigation: train backup Release Manager; document checklist in repo; reduce manual steps via automation

6) Customer expectations creep (“LTS = no behavior changes ever”)
- Mitigation: clear external language; known issues + behavior notes; “mandatory vs optional” patch guidance

11. Dependencies (what can block GA)
Infra/CI
- Release branch secrets + signing key access model finalized (least-privilege)
- Benchmark runner capacity (avoid contention with mainline CI)

Product/Console
- Console: LTS selection/pinning UX, warnings, and release note linking (PM-914 dependency)

Private packaging
- Installer: pin runtime patch tag + verify checksums + documented rollback (ENG-4827)
- Helm: values for LTS channel and release note URL annotations (ENG-4828)

Security/compliance
- SBOM generation: minimum viable output + storage location + verification guidance
- Security patch comms template + SLA alignment

2) Approve reserved perf-canary runner budget for release-branch benchmarks
3) Assign backup Release Manager for LTS (name + % allocation)

13. Success metrics (90 days post-GA)
Customer outcomes
- ≥50% reduction in incident-driven “urgent upgrades” among LTS customers
- Reduced escalation volume related to runtime upgrade regressions (Support)

Engineering outcomes
- Patch train reliability: ≥90% of patches ship on scheduled date
- Mean time to ship critical backport (non-security): <14 days from approval
- Security OOB patch turnaround: within committed SLA (to be finalized)

Business outcomes
- LTS called out as “unblocked” in at least 2 enterprise deals (Sales notes)
- Higher attach rate for Dedicated/Private where change-control is strict

14. Appendix — LTS patch cadence (draft)
Monthly patch schedule (example)
- T-7 days: backport slate freeze + perf baseline run
- T-5 days: candidate RC build + full CI/perf suite
- T-2 days: SRE readiness review + sign-offs
- T day: publish artifacts + release notes; begin controlled rollout
- T+1 to T+7: monitor SLOs; collect pilot feedback; file follow-ups

Emergency security patch
- Separate track with expedited approvals
- Mandatory comms to Support/CS/Sales + affected customers
- Postmortem + backport process audit
